practices.title: No third-party dependencies
practices.what: Every primitive (base64, PEM, DER, the hashes, the fields and curves, argument parsing) is implemented in the repository. proptest is used only by tests, and libfuzzer-sys only by the fuzz targets.
practices.check: make check-no-deps fails if a third-party crate reaches a normal or build dependency.

practices.title: unsafe in one module
practices.what: The workspace denies unsafe code. The one exception is the operating system's random number interface, in baldssl-crypto's os_rng module.
practices.check: make check-unsafe fails on unsafe anywhere else.

practices.title: Output identical to OpenSSL
practices.what: Commands print what OpenSSL prints, byte for byte; an input baldssl cannot print exactly is rejected as unsupported rather than printed differently.
practices.check: Golden files recorded from OpenSSL 3.0.22, 3.5.9 and 4.1.0, and a live differential test against OpenSSL 3.0.22, 3.5.9, 3.6.5, 4.0.3 and 4.1.0, in both directions.

practices.title: Laws as property tests
practices.what: Each structure is a trait whose laws are stated in its documentation: the field and group axioms, the isomorphisms between curve models, the scalar multiplication as a module action, and the round trip and canonicity of every encoding.
practices.check: Each law is a generic property test that every implementation runs.

practices.title: Known answers from the specifications
practices.what: Test vectors come from the standards and from OpenSSL (FIPS 180-4, RFC 4648, RFC 8032, SEC 2, key pairs generated by OpenSSL), not from baldssl's own output.

practices.title: Strict, canonical decoding
practices.what: Decoders accept exactly one encoding of each value: DER rather than BER, canonical base64, field elements below the modulus, points on the curve.
practices.check: Canonicity tests over arbitrary byte strings, and fuzzing.

practices.title: Constant time by construction
practices.what: Predicates on secret data return a Choice, not a bool, and selection replaces branching. Constant-time and variable-time group laws are distinct traits, so a variable-time implementation cannot reach a secret. This is a design discipline, not yet a verified property.
practices.check: Code review and the type system.

practices.title: Fuzzing, mutation testing, coverage
practices.what: Fuzz targets for base64, PEM, DER and X.509; mutation testing reports the mutants no test kills; test coverage is measured.
practices.check: Fuzzing daily and mutation testing weekly in CI; coverage on every run.

practices.title: Strict lints, three toolchains
practices.what: Clippy's pedantic set, with unwrap, expect, panic, indexing and unchecked arithmetic denied; the toolchain is pinned, and the tests run on Rust stable, beta and nightly.
practices.check: make lint, in CI on each toolchain.

practices.title: Conventions checked, not remembered
practices.what: Trait bounds are written in where clauses, imports sit at the top of their module and never inside a function or block, and the code mentions no issue or pull request: it describes itself.
practices.check: make check-where-clauses and make check-use-at-top, in CI.

practices.title: Every citation linked
practices.what: Every standard, paper and formula cited in the code links its source, down to the section.
practices.check: make check-urls checks every URL in the sources and in the rendered API documentation, including the anchors.

practices.title: One source for each table
practices.what: The command, building-block and platform tables are data files: the website renders them, and CI builds its platform matrix from the same file.
practices.check: A test fails if the command table and the binary disagree; the site build fails if a listed item has no tracking issue.

practices.title: Prepared for formal verification
practices.what: The core crates are written in the Rust subset Aeneas extracts to Lean 4, and a Lean project is built against the pinned Aeneas library.
practices.check: make check-aeneas and the Lean build, in CI.

practices.title: Small reviewed steps
practices.what: Features land as stacked pull requests, one primitive each, with CI green before the next. Each pull request updates the website, and each planned item is tracked by an issue.
